investigation.title: Remote Agents: Swarm Gateway 502 Blocking All Agent Provisioning Evals (production-api)
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents feature checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-09-10T16:27–16:28Z with an identical 502 bad_gateway error indicating the swarm gateway ELB endpoint was unreachable during agent provisioning. Because the failure occurs at the POST /api/agents call before any agent identity or VM state is returned, zero required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) were collected, causing a complete contract gap for all three checks.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm gateway — an AWS ELB in us-east-2 fronting the /v1/agents provisioning endpoint — was unreachable at the time of the eval run. The production-api layer returned HTTP 502 with code "bad_gateway" on every POST /api/agents attempt across all three sibling checks, preventing agent creation from starting and leaving all required evidence fields unpopulated. The failure is localized to the swarm gateway / ELB layer, not to the eval runner logic or the expected-output contract definitions. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence; this is an eval-detected infrastructure availability issue.

investigation.title: image-generation-stream Eval Failure: OpenAI API Credit Balance Exhausted on /api/generate/image/stream
investigation.summary: The image-generation-stream observability eval failed because the OpenAI API key used by the eval runner has no remaining credits, causing the upstream image generation request to be rejected with error code credit_balance_exhausted. The stream terminated with a generation_error frame instead of the required generation_completed frame, so both contract assertions failed: frameTypes did not contain generation_completed and imageUrlPresent remained false.
investigation.rootCause: The OpenAI account associated with the API key used by the eval runner at /api/generate/image/stream has exhausted its credit balance. The OpenAI API returned HTTP error type insufficient_quota / code credit_balance_exhausted, which the AURA backend translated into a generation_error SSE frame with code GENERATION_FAILED. Because the generation was aborted before completion, no generation_completed frame was emitted and no image artifact URL was produced, causing both required contract assertions to fail. This is an eval infrastructure / external dependency failure; no evidence of user-traffic or production incident signals is present in the packet.
proof: failed-check.message: OpenAI error type=insufficient_quota code=credit_balance_exhausted surfaced verbatim in the check failure message and in the generation_error frame payload.

failed-check.timing: latencyMs=2279, well below the warningLatencyMs=180000 threshold, confirming the request was rejected immediately by OpenAI rather than timing out.

expected-output.contract: contract requires frameTypes contains generation_completed AND imageUrlPresent equals true (infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json lines 339-344); both assertions violated.

Secondary: The API key used by the eval runner belongs to a different OpenAI organization or project than intended, one whose quota is exhausted, while the intended account still has credits.
Tertiary: A spending limit or rate cap was applied to the OpenAI account or the specific API key, causing it to behave as if credits are exhausted even if the account balance is non-zero.
